summary.headline: ACME Solar Q2 FY27 revenue rose 67.5% YoY to INR1,007 crore; FY27 BESS commissioning guidance raised to over 12 GWh.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue of INR1,007 crore (up 67.5% YoY) and EBITDA of INR874 crore (up 63.6%) were driven mainly by short-term peak power BESS operations and renewable additions. PAT rose 133.5% YoY to INR269 crore, a 26.7% margin. Management raised FY27 BESS commissioning guidance to more than 12 GWh from 10 GWh and lifted its 2030 target to 15 GW renewable plus 50 GWh BESS. Partial commissioning reached 1.9 GW, but full commissioning depends on GNA/substation timelines, which remain the main execution risk.

segments.name: Renewable generation
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin 90.8%; CUF improved to 27.8% from 24.1%; about 150 MW wind added, which ran at around 41% CUF in the quarter.

segments.name: BESS (peak power)
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin 78.3%; about 5.2 GWh commissioned, described as second largest in India; 324 million units sold under short-term contracts.

guidance_outlook: FY27 BESS commissioning guidance raised to more than 12 GWh from 10 GWh.
FY27 renewable capacity target around 1.5 GW, possibly slipping by a quarter depending on Fatehgarh-II GNA; partial commissioning could reach 2.5-3 GW.
FY28 capacity addition guided at 2.5-3 GW, with most substations expected to go live June to December 2028.
By 2030, renewable target raised to 15 GW (from 10 GW) and BESS to 50 GWh (from 25 GWh); management says contracted capacity could reach that level by end of calendar 2027.
H2 FY27 capex expected to be similar to or above the INR6,500 crore spent in H1, per management; exact figure to be shared later.
Contracted revenue: over INR1,600 crore locked for partial FY27 capacity and over INR1,500 crore for FY28; FY27 BESS about 90-95% tied up, FY28 about 50-65%.
capex_capacity: Approximately 5.2 GWh of BESS commissioned to date; 5 GWh half-yearly target achieved.
1.9 GW of contracted projects partially commissioned; 1.7 GW of modules delivered to site, of which 1.1 GW installed and 200 MWp charged.
About 19 GWh of BESS contracted with CATL, Hithium, Ganfeng, Trina and CLOU; about 7 GWh at sites and 5 GWh with LCs opened but not yet received.
BESS capex below INR1 crore per MWh (about INR90 lakh to INR1 crore), helped by installing at operational substations, saving about INR20 lakh per MWh.
Fatehgarh-II has about 700 MWp installed awaiting GNA; Neemuch, Bikaner-III and Ananthapur are the next projects.
demand_pricing: Near-term peak power bids are priced substantially above realisations seen so far, per management; Q2 and Q3 tariffs were already contracted.
Management cites an RTC-to-BESS shift: 85% of DEEP portal short- and medium-term volumes are thermal RTC tenders; RTC at about INR7 or INR6 versus BESS at about INR10.
SECI launched a 4 GW / 16 GWh auction for 4-hour assured peak power with VGF of INR15 lakh per MWh and 12-month commissioning.
Pipeline of 20+ GW upcoming tenders across solar+BESS, FDRE, CfD and PHSP; 50 GWh of peak power bids rolled out to 27 September; 200-250 GWh of short-term contracts expected.
Lithium carbonate prices have fallen, copper has risen and a 6% Chinese export tax applies from January; management expects battery prices to decline further.
Module prices for ALMM List-II compliant DCR modules quoted below INR17 per Wp; procurement planned from June 2027 for December 2027 to March 2028 commissioning.
NTPC 400 MW FDRE PPA signed; tariff reduced about INR0.33 per unit (INR0.11 tentative change in law, INR0.22 voluntary); battery increased to 4.5 hours from 4.

qa_highlights.question: Revised FY27 capacity additions, capex and capitalisation plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 1.5 GW of full commissioning in FY27 (could slip a quarter); H1 capex about INR6,500 crore, with a similar or higher H2 spend. Whole 12 GWh BESS to be capitalised in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why is H2 capex guidance only INR12,000 crore against earlier INR15,000-17,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 capex will be higher than INR6,500 crore, since about 7 GWh of batteries are already at site and 5 GWh more is under LCs. No GNA dependency for battery installs.

qa_highlights.question: Why does 1.9 GW partial commissioning not reconcile with 324 million units of BESS sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 25% CUF benchmark applies only to the solar portion. Bikaner has 133 MW charged out of 300 MW, with about 90-100 MW AC charging BESS and 33-40 MW supplied to clients. Management will add the configuration table in future presentations.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross block rise about INR1,782 crore QoQ while operational debt rose about INR3,100 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross debt rose to about INR26,500 crore from INR20,000 crore, partly from refinancing and partly from early disbursements for battery LCs. Rest went into CWIP; some debt drawn at quarter-end sits as cash of about INR10,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 15 GW target face grid connectivity risk and is it realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said substation timelines of 2028 to early 2029 carry buffer for 6-12 months of delay. It has 8.5 GW of PPAs and expects 3-4 GW more soon, targeting 12 GW contracted by 2029 and 15 GW by 2030, with the tie-ups achievable by end of calendar 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost stay flat and how is cost of debt set to move?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the INR2,800 crore QIP paydown, internal accruals reducing debt drawdown, and refinancing of higher-rate bonds; the book is 100% rupee. About 65% of debt is from PFC, REC, IREDA and NaBFID, with roughly INR10,000 crore of the INR15,000 crore operational book not expected to see rate hikes.

risks_watch: GNA and substation delays: full commissioning of FDRE/hybrid plants depends on GNA going live; FY27 target could slip by a quarter.
Power purchase cost: no tie-up for buying power; BESS charging relies on IEX prices until own solar is ready, with the mix to be disclosed next quarter.
BESS spread compression: Q2 contracts were already signed, but management expects new bids at higher tariffs; watch for narrowing as new BESS capacity arrives.
Lumpy debt and capitalisation timing: debt drawn ahead of LC and installation, which could widen the gap between gross debt and gross block.
Battery and module cost: Chinese export tax from January and cell supply in India for ALMM List-II compliance.
Pending clarifications: BESS and solar commissioning table and the exact H2 capex figure were promised but not yet provided.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, pricing and the raised targets, but noticeably hedged on GNA-linked commissioning timelines ("could be more, could be less by a quarter"). Several answers were defensive on capex and commissioning reconciliation, and some numbers were promised for later disclosure.
key_quotes: We are raising our targets across all three time frames.
Given our execution momentum and the scale of the opportunity, we are raising our targets across all three time frames.
BESS is a new form of power which has developed trust with now maybe 10 to 12 governments.
15 gigawatt is not at risk in terms of the GNA connectivity, because the substations we are targeting for these 15 gigawatts have a timeline of 2028 at last and maybe early 2029.

rows.label: FY28 contracted revenue and PPA build-out
